paper_metadata.title: Education Level and Long-Term Mortality, Recurrent Stroke, and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Ischemic Stroke

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study utilizes a large sample from a well-defined multicenter trial (CATIS) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and high participation rates. Baseline characteristics are extensively described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: This study was conducted among patients from the CATIS (China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke), a multicenter, single-blind randomized controlled clinical trial performed among 4071 patients with acute ischemic stroke.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly identified as participants of the CATIS trial across 26 hospitals.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Eligible participants were ≥22 years old, had ischemic stroke confirmed by computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging within 48 hours of symptom onset, and had an elevated systolic blood pressure (BP) between 140 and <220 mm Hg.
items.reasoning: Recruitment methods and diagnostic confirmation (CT/MRI) are explicitly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The CATIS trial excluded patients with a BP ≥220/120 mm Hg, severe heart failure, acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina, atrial fibrillation, aortic dissection, serious cerebrovascular stenosis (≥70%), or resistant hypertension and those in a deep coma.
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are provided, including clinical and diagnostic parameters.

items.reasoning: Out of 4071 original trial participants, 3861 (94.8%) were included, which is well above the 80% threshold for low risk.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (education) was measured using a validated questionnaire and categorized clearly. Sensitivity analyses using years of education as a continuous/tertile variable support the robustness of the measurement.

items.reasoning: The categories are clearly defined and standard.
